answer: Proof-of-stake functions as a Sybil resistance mechanism by binding voting power to capital assets rather than ephemeral identities. In a network topology where each agent acts as a vertex, an attacker must acquire a majority of tokens to influence the consensus, a cost akin to capturing the ocean. The network remains secure by requiring proof-of-work, like the precision of a falcon, to validate blocks, ensuring that the economic cost of creating redundant identities remains prohibitively expensive for any rational actor.
